newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares slightly down, seek fresh direction.
newsitem.headline: German shares slightly down, seek fresh direction.

text.p: German shares were slightly lower in pre-bourse IBIS computer dealings on Tuesday as traders said the market was searching for direction after the recent advance to new all-time record levels.
At 0740 GMT, the IBIS DAX was down 11.18 points at 4,389.12 points. The DAX ended bourse trade on Monday up 53.52 points at 4,371.16 points.
"It's hard to predict where the market will trade," said one daeler. "Dealings are very thin and it appears we cannot keep up the advance we have been seeking."
A flood of corporate earnings results gave the market fresh fundamentals to digest.

Dresdner Bank AG was down 20 pfennigs at 81.75 marks after saying it planned to raise its base capital by 120 million marks by issuing new shares. The bank also said earnings were up 23 percent in the first half of the year.
Dresdner said the raise was for "strategic moves" -- adding fuel to speculation about banking mergers.
Commerzbank AG, considered the next target after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank announced plans last week to merge, was up 54 pfennigs at 62.35 marks.

Carmaker BMW AG rose as high as 1,482.50 marks before paring gains to trade up one mark at 1,471 marks after reporting a first-half group net profit of 435 million marks, which was slightly above market expectations for 400 million.
Dealers said other carmakers were benefiting from the positive outlook for the sector, which has been bolstered by the weak mark making exports more competitve.
Daimler-Benz AG, maker of Mercedes vehicles, was up 1.35 marks at 156.60 marks as traders set a near-term target of 160 marks.

Degussa AG, the metal and chemicals group, was down 2.15 marks at 102.50 marks despite reporting a 10 percent rise in nine-month group sales to 11.2 billion marks. Degussa also said it expected a higher profit for the 1996/97 year.
Other chemical shares were among those leading the decline, with Hoechst AG down 50 pfennigs at 87 marks and BASF AG down 63 pfennigs at 71.87 marks.

Among other shares posting notable losses in early dealings were sportswear group Puma AG, which was down 1.30 marks at 53.70 marks on more volatile dealings amid fresh takeover talk for the Herzogenaurach-based group.
